we present a model for transactional memory that is both expressive enough to capture all existing transactional memory systems (including the widely-used TSO and x86-TSO), and also expressive enough to support a wide variety of new transactional memory features.

The main takeaway from our work is that
transactional memory is not just a useful programming abstraction, but also an effective basis for building new abstractions.
transactional memory, when properly designed, can offer far more powerful concurrency abstractions than have previously been possible.
